LEVELS ARE STRUCTURE, NOT ARITHMETIC: every level I hand on is either a prior 52-week high/low that actually traded, or a moving average derived from finviz's own relative-distance figure (price / (1 + pct/100)). brazil_story.day2_bias:
Monday was DAY 1 of the gap (the attack was Sat/Sun, so Monday's cash session already priced the surprise). Tuesday is DAY 2. The two legs behave DIFFERENTLY and must be split — treating them as one theme is the mistake available here.

LEG 1 — CRUDE AND ENERGY PRODUCERS: base case GAP-AND-FADE on the attack headline itself. The generic pattern after a geopolitical supply surprise is that the risk premium decays on day 2 unless fresh physical damage is confirmed (LABELLED: pattern is FROM MEMORY, NOT web-verified). The instance-specific evidence IS sourced and supports the fade: Saudi refineries operational, Russia releasing 300,000+ tons / 2.25M barrels of diesel with more to follow, ICE diesel futures already -2.3% to $1,449/ton, the IEA pushing members to accelerate releases, and a Russia-Ukraine energy-infrastructure ceasefire announced Sunday. Monday priced a threat to supply that has not yet materialised in barrels. Confidence MODERATE, undermined by an un-timed OPEC report.

LEG 2 — SPECULATIVE / HIGH-BETA RISK-OFF (quantum, SMRs, mortgage finance, fintech, semis): base case CONTINUATION, not reversal. The reason is mechanical — this leg was not driven by a one-off surprise in those names, it was driven by RATES, and the rate driver is still fully in force AND HAS NOT FINISHED PRICING, because the bond market was closed while it happened. Yields at 24-year highs, 20.5% October hike odds, ~87.6% by December, dollar at an 18-month high. Reversals in this complex under that backdrop are intraday bounces, not day-trends. Confidence HIGHER than Leg 1, because the driver is observable and still present rather than decaying. The orchestrator's warning stands and I reinforce it: a long in the high-beta AI/quantum/SMR complex Tuesday fights BOTH Monday's flow AND an un-priced bond reopen.

LEG 3 — TANKERS AND SHIPPING (DHT +6.41%, FRO +5.51% Monday, both on the watchlist): base case CONTINUATION, and the one place the day-2 fade does NOT apply. The orchestrator is right that this is a freight-rate story, not a crude-price story, and that distinction is the whole point: freight and insurance rates do not mean-revert when the attack headline cools, they ratchet with route risk. OPEC+ puts shipping and insurance above one third of cargo value; 10+ VLCCs are refusing the Gulf. A crude fade can coexist with rising tanker rates. CAVEAT: both already moved 5-6% on day 1, so a day-2 entry is a chase into an extended move; with every setup at 'sample' status in the expectancy table, that sizes at DEFAULT at best and more honestly at low confidence.

WHAT FLIPS EACH:
- Flips Leg 1 fade -> CONTINUATION: a new attack with confirmed damage to Saudi PRODUCTION or EXPORT capacity rather than an airport; a Hormuz closure or a tanker sinking; Brent decisively clearing Monday's $105.91 high; or the OPEC report cutting supply guidance. Any one and the fade is dead.
- Deepens Leg 1 fade: confirmation Russian diesel volumes are landing, or the energy ceasefire holding (Zelenskyy accused Russia of violating it Monday — live and two-sided).
- Flips Leg 2 continuation -> BOUNCE, and this is THE thing to watch Tuesday morning: the 10Y cash market reopening BID, back under roughly 5.20%, ideally alongside a bank beat. That removes the duration pressure doing the actual damage. A dollar reversal off its 18-month high corroborates. Absent BOTH, do not buy the dip in the speculative complex.
- Flips Leg 3: de-escalation that reopens the Gulf to the VLCCs that turned away, or insurance rates visibly rolling over. Neither is in evidence tonight.
